facts.text: Trailing-twelve-month revenue is ₹3.60 lakh cr, +4% on the prior twelve months.
Trailing-twelve-month PAT is ₹83,685 cr, +12% on the prior twelve months.
Sep 2026 quarter: revenue ₹95,132 cr (+9% YoY), PAT ₹21,537 cr (+6% YoY).
Revenue has compounded at 19% over 10 years, 22% over 5 and 27% over 3; the last twelve months (+4%) are running behind the 3-year pace.
Profit has compounded slower than revenue over 3 years (18% vs 27%).
Quarterly revenue growth has accelerated over the last four quarters: +2% → +0% → +4% → +9% YoY.
Deposits stand at ₹33.24 lakh cr, +7% since Mar 2026.
Assets are 8.6× shareholders' equity (₹6.03 lakh cr); leverage is the business model for a lender, so watch asset quality rather than debt.
Foreign institutions hold 39.4%, −9.0 pp over a year.
Operating cash flow is not a useful quality test for a lender — deposits and loans flow through it. Judge earnings quality on asset quality and provisioning instead.

claims.claim: Q2 margins are the bottom for the bank.
claims.quote: by all account, Parag, that is what we were alluding to, to say that the rate cycle having already kicked in earlier in October, that is a good tailwind

claims.claim: The bank's liquidity is extremely comfortable.
claims.quote: a low LCR does not mean a low liquidity. The liquidity is extremely comfortable.

claims.claim: Cost of funds remained flat sequentially.
claims.quote: our cost of funds is flat quarter-to-quarter, at about 4.4% last quarter to this quarter. Sequentially, it has remained flat.

claims.claim: The bank continues to gain market share in deposits on both an incremental and stock basis.
claims.quote: We continue to gain market share both on an incremental basis and on a stock basis as well.

claims.claim: The bank believes cost of funds benefit is an opportunity that will play out over time.
claims.quote: the cost of funds is the biggest opportunity on the margin where compared to our historical norms as well as compared to what we have seen in the industry as such, there can be 40, 50 basis points change

claims.claim: The bank expects to mute incremental investments in distribution while continuing technology investments.
claims.quote: you will see a whilst investments will be slightly muted, especially in distribution for now, but technology we’re continuing because security and AI is going to be a very significant part

claims.claim: The bank is seeing healthy credit demand in the system.
claims.quote: There is a very healthy credit demand that we are seeing in the system as we speak.

claims.claim: The bank has consistently gained market share on deposits by 30 to 50 basis points annually over the last 5 years.
claims.quote: We have demonstrated our ability to gain market share on deposits every year, almost around 30 to 50 basis points over the last 5 years.

claims.claim: The bank holds 35% to 40% of account settlements in the Capital Markets segment.
claims.quote: In the Capital Markets segment, we continue to hold about 35% to 40% of the account settlements.

claims.claim: The bank holds 40% to 50% of escrow settlements in the bankers to issue business.
claims.quote: in the bankers to issue we hold about 40% to 50% of the escrow settlement.

claims.claim: The bank processes 26% to 28% of total market card spends.
claims.quote: In the spends, almost 26% to 28% of the card spends in the market is through our cards.

claims.claim: The bank's return on assets remained stable at 1.9% due to cost efficiencies.
claims.quote: Despite the drop in NIMs, the return on assets continue to be stable at 1.9% due to cost efficiencies

claims.claim: The bank has created a large provisioning buffer of 125 basis points to absorb future shocks.
claims.quote: The bank has created a large provisioning buffer of almost 125 basis points to absorb any shocks in the future

claims.claim: The bank's asset quality continues to be pristine with no particular segment showing major signs of concern.
claims.quote: I would say the asset quality continues at the bank to be pristine. And as we see it, there is no particular segment which is showing any major signs of concern.

claims.claim: The bank is addressing competition through relationships rather than pricing.
claims.quote: we are addressing competition only through relationship and not through pricing.

claims.claim: The bank's auto loans are over 80% self-funded by customer liability accounts.
claims.quote: I do want to let you know that our auto loans are almost a little more than 80% self-funded

claims.claim: NIM compressed by 8 basis points due to front-loading of interest rate cuts on the asset side.
claims.quote: As expected, due to the front loading of the interest rate cuts on the asset side of the balance sheet, we did see NIM compress by about 8 basis points.

claims.claim: The bank expects NIMs to improve over the next 6 to 12 months as deposit repricing provides a tailwind.
claims.quote: We should see over the next 6 to 12 months the deposit repricing having some amount of tailwind effect in the NIMs.

claims.claim: The bank continues to see market share gains in deposits.
claims.quote: We continue to see market share gains in deposits and we are very focused and disciplined in pricing.

claims.claim: The bank added approximately Rs 1,600 crores in contingent provisions during the quarter.
claims.quote: at an aggregate level, the contingent provisions have been added by about Rs.1,600 crores or so.

claims.claim: The bank has reduced turnaround time for salaried home loans to two days and self-employed to three days.
claims.quote: For salaried loans, we have now brought down the turnaround time to two days and for self-employed, it is about three days.

claims.claim: Quarterly fluctuations in margins are expected due to the lead-lag impact of rate changes on assets versus liabilities.
claims.quote: Whilst we may see quarterly fluctuations in margins due to this lead lag impact, we expect to stabilize it over a period of time.

claims.claim: The bank successfully reduced its credit-deposit ratio from 110% at the time of merger to about 95% currently.
claims.quote: bring down the CD / credit deposit ratio from 110% at the time of merger to about 95% as we speak today.

claims.claim: The bank grew average deposits at 16% year-on-year last year and continued to gain market share.
claims.quote: Last year, we have grown our average deposits at a healthy pace of 16% year-on-year and continued to gain market share as we have done in the past.

claims.claim: The bank's asset side is approximately 70% floating rate, while the liability side is mostly fixed.
claims.quote: A large part of our asset side of the balance sheet is floating in nature. It's somewhere around the 70%, and whilst the liability side is more or less fixed in nature.

claims.claim: The bank's retail NPA (excluding agri) is stable at 82 basis points, consistent with the same period last year.
claims.quote: if you look at the NPA on the retail segment excluding agri, it’s at about 82 basis points. Last year, same time, it was 82 basis points.

synthesis.one_liner: HDFC Bank delivers steady profit growth alongside accelerating quarterly revenue, though management continues to avoid specific quantitative targets.

narrative_vs_numbers.says: Management emphasizes ongoing market share gains in deposits and healthy credit demand across the system.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: Trailing twelve month revenue is ₹3.60 lakh cr (+4% YoY), while quarterly revenue growth accelerated to 9% YoY at ₹95,132 cr.

narrative_vs_numbers.says: Management claims return on assets remained stable due to cost efficiencies and that margins have bottomed.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: Trailing twelve month PAT reached ₹83,685 cr, up 12% YoY, while Sep 2026 quarter PAT grew 6% YoY to ₹21,537 cr.

narrative_vs_numbers.says: Management offers various targets for loan growth, LCR ranges, and credit-deposit ratios across earnings calls.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: The ledger scores zero out of thirteen guidance items as delivered, with all items currently unmeasured or untestable against financials.

synthesis.credibility: Management has zero verifiable delivered promises out of thirteen tracked guidance items, frequently deflecting analyst pressures on margins, deposit growth, and credit costs while leaving targets unmeasured.

bull.evidence: Quarterly revenue growth accelerated over the last four quarters from 2% to 9% YoY.
Trailing twelve month PAT reached ₹83,685 cr, representing a 12% increase.
Total deposits stand at ₹33.24 lakh cr, growing 7% since March 2026.

bear.evidence: Trailing twelve month revenue growth of 4% trails the 3-year compound rate of 27%.
Profit compounded at 18% over 3 years, lagging behind revenue's 27% compound rate.
Foreign institutional holdings declined by 9.0 percentage points over the year to 39.4%.

watch: Check if quarterly revenue growth sustains its 9% YoY pace in the next results.
Monitor deposit growth relative to the stated LCR target range of 110 to 120 percent.
